speaker: Doctor
text: Tell me, what exactly happened during the rear-end collision, and were you wearing a seatbelt? Did you hear or feel a loud pop or snap in your hip or groin at the moment of impact?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the specific position your right leg is currently in, and are you able to actively lift your knee against gravity? REQUEST TEST: Hip_X-Ray. REQUEST IMAGES: Hip_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The right leg is positioned in slight shortening, flexion, adduction, and internal rotation. Active lifting of the knee against gravity is limited due to pain and abnormal positioning. Hip_X-Ray Findings: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
